2610.08208.title: STRUCTURALCOST: A controlled reading time dataset for modeling human sentence processing difficulty
2610.08208.paper_summary: We introduce STRUCTURALCOST, a self-paced reading dataset of 475 participants and 40,800 observations isolating the processing cost of long-distance subject-verb dependency resolution. We replicate a low-powered psycholinguistic finding at NLP scale, namely that human reading times at the main verb increase with dependency length, driven by syntactic embedding beyond linear distance. Different language models -- spanning n-gram models, SSMs, and transformers -- partially mirror this graded difficulty profile, yet underestimate the integration cost humans incur, with a gap that persists across architectures and model sizes. This suggests these models capture the predictive component of human processing but not the full integration cost that working memory imposes. STRUCTURALCOST provides data needed to drive progress toward evaluating the cognitive plausibility of language models.
2610.08208.paper_summary_zh: 我們介紹了STRUCTURALCOST，一個包含475名參與者和40,800個觀察值的自我調整閱讀數據集，旨在隔離長距離主謂依賴解析的處理成本。我們在NLP規模上複製了一個低效能的心理語言學發現，即人類在主要動詞的閱讀時間隨著依賴長度的增加而增加，這是由超越線性距離的句法嵌入驅動的。不同的語言模型——涵蓋n-gram模型、SSMs和Transformer——部分反映了這種分級難度特徵，但低估了人類所承擔的整合成本，這一差距在不同架構和模型大小中持續存在。這表明這些模型捕捉到了人類處理的預測組件，但未能捕捉到工作記憶所施加的完整整合成本。STRUCTURALCOST提供了推進評估語言模型認知合理性所需的數據。
